newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles $2.4 billion school bond measure fails.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles $2.4 billion school bond measure fails.

text.p: A $2.4 billion bond measure that would finance repairs and construction for the Los Angeles Unified School District failed to receive the required two-thirds vote, according to election returns.

Proposition BB, which would have required a property tax increase of on average $38.56 per $100,000 of assessed valuation, received 65.71 percent of the vote, just short of the 66 percent it would have required to pass.
"We're talking about losing by a whisker," said Leon Wozniak, a district spokesman. "There's always hope with the absentee ballots."

A related measure, called Proposition AA, which would have provided $205 million for lighting and landscaping at nine Los Angeles community colleges, also failed, receiving only 48.5 percent of the vote.
